messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED: prefill GPU memory exhaustion on rwd-prod-usw2 (severity: high). Auto-snooze disabled. Pager routed to #incidents. Playbook: https://wiki.redwood.io/ops/prefill-oom

alice_oncall: I’m on it. Seeing container restarts on gpu-pool-usw2-b (node ids 42/43/44). Symptoms: CUDA OOM during prefill for long-context requests.

ben_sre: Can you paste the relevant log lines? rough surface area: which models/routes?

alice_oncall: paste logs below — repeated pattern at prefill step then container restart:
```
[2026-03-17T03:12:04Z] model_runner.cpp:427 PrefillTokens=126432 Allocating KV cache...
[2026-03-17T03:12:04Z] cuda: ERROR cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (err 2)
[2026-03-17T03:12:04Z] runtime: container restart (exit code 137)
[2026-03-17T03:12:05Z] orchestrator: rescheduled pod rwd-model-abc-xx to gpu-pool-usw2-b-43
```

priya_runtime: Affected route is `generate-large-context` (model: open-llm-32k-q4). Observed prefill token counts >> configured guardrail. KVCACHE growth + large seqs are hitting per-GPU memory ceiling.

jules_support: Customer visibility: AcmeCorp (enterprise, heavy long-context usage) reported 503s starting ~03:12 UTC. Support ticket #INC-8721 opened. They say it was during a batch of very long prompts.

omar_platform: Quick mitigation options: 1) enforce PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS env to 8192 for vulnerable pools, 2) enable aggressive kvcache eviction, 3) route >16k token requests to coldmodel fallback (CPU). I can roll the env change to gpu-pool-usw2-b now.

alice_oncall: Do the env change. Also enable temporary rate-limit on `generate-large-context` for hosted tier to reduce surge.

omar_platform: Running rollout:
```
$ rctl pool update gpu-pool-usw2-b --env PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=8192 --env KV_EVICTION=aggressive --no-wait
rollout id: rdo-20260317-001
```
Started applying hotpatch to pool.

ben_sre: Noted. I’ll watch for node flaps — we saw one driver reset earlier that coincided with a kernel OOM. If nodes keep resetting we may need to cordon and reboot.

priya_runtime: Also flipping on short-term fallback for prefill failures to avoid hard crashes: set PREFILL_FALLBACK=swap-to-coldmodel. This will increase latency but avoid restarts. Command:
```
runtimectl set-policy generate-large-context fallback=coldmodel threshold=1
```

omar_platform: Hotpatch applied to envs. Initial metrics: OOM restarts dropped by ~60% within 2 minutes. However gpu-pool-usw2-b-44 shows a driver reset and ephemeral node flapping.

alice_oncall: Ben, can you take the node? cordon then drain and reboot? I’ll continue customer comms.

ben_sre: On it. `kubectl cordon gpu-pool-usw2-b-44 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` Reboot triggered.

jules_support: Sent interim customer update to AcmeCorp: "We're mitigating large-context prefill memory pressure; generators may be slower as we route to cold fallback. We'll follow up after stabilization." Customer appreciated the heads-up.

tracy_pm: Is there measurable customer impact beyond AcmeCorp? Any higher-severity SLAs hit?

alice_oncall: Brief summary of metrics 03:10-04:10 UTC: total request volume unchanged, error rate for `generate-large-context` peaked at 7.4% (baseline ~0.1%). Affected requests mostly >80k prompt tokens. No broad SLA violations for standard routes.

priya_runtime: Root cause preliminary: our guardrail for prefill token budget didn't cap KV cache growth early enough for certain quantized kernels. Also some models have unusually large per-token KV object sizes. Followups: improve early abort on prefill estimate, add dynamic prefill throttling and better quantization mem accounting.

omar_platform: Node reboots finished; pool healthy. Rolling back PREFILL_FALLBACK after stabilization? Or keep for 24h?

alice_oncall: Keep fallback and aggressive eviction for 24h. Schedule postmortem and evals run to reproduce with long prompts. I’ll mark incident resolved when metrics hold for 30m.

ben_sre: FYI, I captured dmesg on the flapping node — driver log indicates a GPU driver reset (see /var/log/kern.log snippet). Will attach to postmortem.

jules_support: Customer notified of final update: we stabilized their traffic, provided timeline, and offered to run a focused eval on their prompt set. They requested a follow-up call.

incident-bot: Incident marked as mitigated by alice_oncall at 6468003600. Postmortem owner requested: priya_runtime. Next steps: postmortem + action items (guardrails, throttling, quantization accounting).

alice_oncall: Thanks everyone. Quick check: capture a sample of failing requests (sanitized) and add to eval corpus. Priya, can you take that?

priya_runtime: Yes — will pull samples into a quarantined eval job and start reproduction tests. Adding action items to the incident board.

alice_oncall: Closing thread here; we’ll follow up in #eng-runtime and the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
